course_name_original: Electrónica Industrial en Sistemas de Generación de Energías Renovables
course_name_en: Industrial Electronics in Renewable Energy Generation Systems
prerequisites: Basic skills and competences in power electronics
Related subjects of the first semester (if basic skills and competences are not covered in student profile/CV)

learning_outcomes.text: Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.
Knowledge of the principal mathematic tools used in the analysis, modelling and simulation of power systems.
Use of computers and digital processors in the analysis, design, simulation, monitoring, control and supervision of power systems.
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Concern for quality and achievement motivation
Understanding of the importance and the area of utilization of electrical power systems for generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy
Characterization, operation and design of electronic topologies and control methods for electric energy conversion
Acquire the basic knowledge of power electronics to analyse and design electrical power systems
Technical-economical-environmental regulations and directives in different scopes (local, regional, national, European, etc.), which are applied to power systems

Knowledge and analysis of the energetic structures and technologies necessary, considering multiple aspects as the requirements, expected technical evolution, efficiency, security, sustainable development concerns, environmental and service guaranteeing issues
Understanding and ability to apply the main particularities and specific techniques of electronic circuits used in power generation systems renewable energy.
Analysis and design of complex power electronics systems, integrating knowledge of different subjects previously viewed.
Comparison and justified selection of devices and power electronic circuits appropriate for a type of generator of renewable energy source (solar, wind, marine, thermal, etc.).
To know where are the margins for the optimization of power generation system, looking for increased performance (efficiency, reduce losses, versatile control, etc.).
To know and select the communication and telemetry system best suited for a particular energy-generating structure.
Practical implementation of control circuits used in power generation systems for renewable energy sources.

syllabus_topics: Specific technologies (Bidirectional converters; association of converters; back-to-back converter; matrix converter; interleaving converters; transformerless converters; modeling of converters; small signal dynamic analysis; ...)
Power electronic circuits for PV generation (input and output characteristics of converters; power topologies; semiconductor technologies; MPPT; drawbacks, solutions and expectations)

Power electronic circuits for Wind generation (input and output characteristics of converters; power topologies; semiconductor technologies; MPPT; modular topologies; drawbacks, solutions and expectations)
1.-Introduction to power electronics in renewable energy systems
1.1.2.- Wind System Basics (Characteristics, technologies, drawbacks and advantages, maximum power point operation)
2. Basic power schemes (DC-DC, DC-AC, AC-DC, AC-AC), Case of Study Wind Systems.
2.1. Diode Bridge + Boost Converter + 3-Phase PWM inverter
3. Advanced power schemes, Case of Study Wind Systems
4. Specific topologies for PV Power Systems
5. Specific Electro Magnetic Compatibility (EMC) Technologies for Renewable Generarion Systems
5.3. Practical issues for PCB Design considering EMC

assessment_methods.method: Written tests (objective tests, short answer tests and / or test development)
Oral tests (individual, group, presentation of topics/projects, etc.)

assessment_rules: The final qualification is calculated from: 40% from works/projects (mandatory), 10% from simulated task performance tests (mandatory), 25% from a comprehensive individual written test at the end of the semester (mandatory, minimum score of 4/10 required), 15% from oral tests, and 10% from attendance to presential hours (minimum 80% required). For part-time students, the 'Observation techniques' mark is not applied, and the total grade is calculated proportionally to the remaining percentages. Oral tests for part-time students will be scheduled on an agreed date, with online presentation available, and other tests may be moved if non-attendance is justified.
